subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical repeated requests, and is a bounded per-reviewer exact-input allow-once-only cache the accepted approval boundary?
rationale: Exec auto-review sits on the process approval boundary, so reusing a prior model verdict changes the one-request-one-review behavior even though the reported duplicate billing bug is real.

options.title: Approve bounded allow-once memo
options.body: Cache only parsed low-risk allow-once decisions inside one reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input, after real configured-run proof is available.

options.title: Cache broader deterministic outcomes
options.body: Permit ask/error/timeout outcomes to be memoized too for more savings, accepting a broader behavior change in the reviewer path.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization for now and accept repeated model cost so every exec request gets a fresh reviewer call.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded allow-once memo
recommendation.body: Cache only parsed low-risk allow-once decisions inside one reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input, after real configured-run proof is available.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle carried much of the normalized exec auto-mode and approval-boundary work in the feature history.
